title: Tensor projection maps respect compact-support composition
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Work on the small etale sites with the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. All schemes mentioned are Noetherian [def-pc-scheme]. Compact-support direct image is the compactification-independent functor of [def-amb-etale-compact-support, lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms admitting compactifications, and let $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For each morphism $a$ write
$$P_{a,Q,B}:Q\otimes_A^LRa_!B\longrightarrow Ra_!(a^*Q\otimes_A^LB)$$
for the tensor projection map obtained from the termwise open-extension tensor map and the proper projection map [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor, def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Let $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ be the proper/open tower-normalized composition comparison of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. Under $(gf)^*K=f^*g^*K$, the actual transformations satisfy
$$\alpha_{g,f,f^*g^*K\otimes M}\circ Rg_!(P_{f,g^*K,M})\circ P_{g,K,Rf_!M}
=P_{gf,K,M}\circ(1_K\otimes\alpha_{g,f,M}).$$
This identity includes compatibility with the proper/open interchange used in the tower and with the refinement comparisons. It holds on the whole ordinary derived categories, without boundedness or finite Tor-amplitude assumptions on $K,M$. Whenever the projection maps are invertible their inverses satisfy the equivalent identity.

proof.text:
Use right-hand tensor factors until the last step. Write $J_j=Dj_!$, $S_h=Rh_*$, $\gamma_j:J_jE\otimes N\to J_j(E\otimes j^*N)$ for the canonical derived open tensor isomorphism, and $\pi_h:S_hE\otimes N\to S_h(E\otimes h^*N)$ for the counit-defined projection map. On $c=(j,r)$ the projection map is
$$t_c=S_r(\gamma_{j;M,r^*N})\circ\pi_{r;J_jM,N}.$$
It first applies the proper projection and then $S_r$ of the open comparison. The map $P$ in the statement is $t_c$ conjugated by the canonical signed tensor symmetry. These maps are defined on arbitrary unbounded inputs; neither $\pi_h$ nor $t_c$ is assumed invertible.

proof.text:
The derived open tensor map restricts to the identity under $j^*J_j\cong1$: the sheaf map has this property, and the derived map is induced from it using a K-flat tensor representative. Thus, for composable opens $j,b$, with the canonical open compositor understood,
$$\gamma_{bj;M,N}=J_b(\gamma_{j;M,b^*N})\circ\gamma_{b;J_jM,N}.$$
Indeed on complexes the two canonical sheaf tensor comparisons both extend the identity of $M\otimes (bj)^*N$ by zero, with the same direct-sum tensor differential. Passing to the derived comparisons preserves this equality. The cited derived tensor lemma already supplies the unbounded comparison; no tensor product of unresolved complexes is being substituted for derived tensor.

proof.text:
For arbitrary composable proper factors use
$$\pi_{vu;E,N}=S_v(\pi_{u;E,v^*N})\circ\pi_{v;S_uE,N}.$$
This is the second identity of the generic projection-composition lemma. Its compositor is the canonical derived direct-image compositor, normalized on K-injective resolutions, so it is the compositor used in compact-support towers. Constant-coefficient inverse image is exact, hence the derived pullbacks in the generic statement are precisely the pullbacks used here. This uses no projection isomorphism.

proof.text:
First prove the mixed square for a CARTESIAN proper/open square $(k:U\to V,r:U\to W,p:V\to Z,i:W\to Z)$. Put $M_N=M\otimes r^*i^*N$ and $\Gamma:J_iS_r\to S_pJ_k$. The desired equality is
$$S_p(\gamma_k)\pi_p(\Gamma_M\otimes1)=\Gamma_{M_N}J_i(\pi_r)\gamma_i.\tag{*}$$
Both arrows have source $J_iS_rM\otimes N\cong J_i(S_rM\otimes i^*N)$ and target $S_pJ_kM_N$. Under $J_i\dashv i^*$, compare their restrictions, then compose with $\lambda_{M_N}:i^*S_pJ_kM_N\to S_rM_N$, the exchange followed by $k^*J_k\cong1$. The interchange node gives $i^*\Gamma_M=\lambda_M^{-1}$. The exchange/tensor coherence node gives, for $E=J_kM$,
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{E\otimes p^*N}\,i^*\pi_p=\pi_r(\operatorname{Ex}_E\otimes1).$$
Restriction of $\gamma_k$ and $\gamma_i$ is the identity by step 2. Consequently the first adjunct becomes $\pi_r(\lambda_M\lambda_M^{-1}\otimes1)=\pi_r$; the second becomes $(\lambda_{M_N}\lambda_{M_N}^{-1})\pi_r=\pi_r$. The adjunction bijection proves (*). All pullback/tensor identifications in this calculation are those of the cited coherence statement.

proof.text:
Now let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be a proper refinement with $uj_1=j_2$, for opens $j_a:X\hookrightarrow T_a$. Put $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$, $b:V\hookrightarrow T_1$, $q:V\to X$, and $s=(j_1,1):X\hookrightarrow V$. The proper-open-section lemma says $s$ is clopen, $qs=1$ and $bs=j_1$; $q$ is proper by the proper-open-p-proper lemma. Factor the refinement square horizontally as
$$(s,1_X,q,1_X)\quad\text{followed by}\quad(b,q,u,j_2).$$
The second square is cartesian. The first is a clopen-section square, which can be noncartesian. The horizontal pasting identity for the SPECIFIED support/K-injective comparisons gives
$$\Gamma_{\rm ref,M}=\Gamma_{\rm cart,J_sM}\circ J_{j_2}(\Gamma_{\rm sec,M}).$$
Thus it remains to check the first square, not to apply the cartesian normalization to it.

For the decomposition $V=s(X)\amalg C$, the cited clopen sheaf-product equivalence also identifies constant-$A$ MODULE sheaves with pairs: an $A$-action and its homomorphisms are specified componentwise. Here $s^*$ is first projection and $s_!=s_*$ is insertion $F\mapsto(F,0)$; both are exact, and $s^*\dashv s_*$ has counit the identity. The same formulas hold for complexes and homotopies. They preserve quasi-isomorphisms, so the localization universal property descends these functors, their inverse equivalences, and their units/counits to the whole unbounded derived categories. The exact-functor-derived lemma identifies $S_s$ with $J_s$, with this normalization. In particular restriction to the two components detects equality of derived arrows; this is an equivalence of categories, not an inference from equality on cohomology or stalks.

proof.text:
Let $J$ be a K-injective representative on $X$. By step 6, $J_sJ=s_*J$ is K-injective: it is the right adjoint of the exact first projection, so the cited K-injective-preservation lemma applies. In the SPECIFIED construction of $\Gamma_{\rm sec}$ choose the resolution $s_!J\to I$ to be the identity with $I=s_!J$. Its support identification is
$$J=1_!1_*J\longrightarrow q_*s_!J=(qs)_*J=J,$$
which is the identity on sections (all support lies in the clopen first component). The derived compositor $c:S_qJ_s\cong S_{qs}=1$ is normalized by these same K-injective representatives. Hence $\Gamma_{\rm sec}=c^{-1}$ as an actual derived transformation, with precisely the support/resolution normalization required in the item.

proof.text: Under $S_s=J_s$, one has $\pi_s=\gamma_s$. In fact the counit definition of $\pi_s$ restricts on $s(X)$ to $1\otimes1$, since $s^*s_*=1$ with identity counit, and it is the unique arrow $0\to0$ on $C$. The canonical $\gamma_s$ has these same two components by step 2. The derived component equivalence of step 6 therefore identifies the arrows. This computation is valid for every derived tensor input, including a nonperfect module over $A=\mathbf Z/4$.

Apply projection composition, step 3, to $X\xrightarrow{s}V\xrightarrow{q}X$ with $qs=1$. Since $\pi_s=\gamma_s$ and $\pi_1=1$, it says
$$c_{M\otimes N}\,S_q(\gamma_s)\pi_q=c_M\otimes1_N.$$
Compose on the right with $\Gamma_{\rm sec,M}\otimes1_N=c_M^{-1}\otimes1_N$ and on the left with $c_{M\otimes N}^{-1}$. The result is
$$S_q(\gamma_s)\pi_q(\Gamma_{\rm sec,M}\otimes1_N)=\Gamma_{\rm sec,M\otimes N}.$$
This is exactly (*) for $(s,1,q,1)$: the other route has $\gamma_1=\pi_1=1$. Thus the noncartesian part of every refinement respects tensor, with the specified arrow, without any invertibility claim for $\pi_q$.

proof.text:
Combine the two factors of the refinement in step 5. More explicitly, substitute $\Gamma_{\rm ref}=\Gamma_{\rm cart}J_s\circ J_{j_2}\Gamma_{\rm sec}$ into the left side of (*), and expand $\gamma_{j_1}=\gamma_{bs}$ by step 2. Apply the cartesian identity of step 4 with input $J_sM$; naturality moves $\Gamma_{\rm sec,M}$ through its open tensor map. The remaining interior composite is $S_q(\gamma_s)\pi_q(\Gamma_{\rm sec,M}\otimes1)$, which step 9 replaces by $\Gamma_{\rm sec,M\otimes j_2^*N}$. Horizontal pasting then recombines the two factors into $\Gamma_{\rm ref,M\otimes j_2^*N}$. This proves the fully typed refinement identity
$$S_u(\gamma_{j_1;M,u^*N})\pi_{u;J_{j_1}M,N}(\Gamma_{\rm ref,M}\otimes1)
=\Gamma_{\rm ref,M\otimes j_2^*N}\gamma_{j_2;M,N}.$$
Its source is $J_{j_2}M\otimes N$ and target is $S_uJ_{j_1}(M\otimes j_2^*N)$, using $j_1^*u^*N=j_2^*N$.

source.place: Tag 0F7D, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal; pasting the explicit tensor identities of steps 4 and 9

proof.text:
For compactifications $a=r_1j_1=r_2j_2$ with $r_1=r_2u$, the refinement comparison is $\rho=S_{r_2}\Gamma_{\rm ref}$ followed by the direct-image compositor. Apply step 10 with $N=r_2^*Q$, then $S_{r_2}$, and precompose with $\pi_{r_2}$. Naturality of $\pi_{r_2}$ moves $\Gamma_{\rm ref}\otimes1$ past it, and step 3 combines $\pi_{r_2}$ and $\pi_u$ into $\pi_{r_1}$. By the definition in step 1 the resulting equality is
$$t_{c_1;M,Q}(\rho_M\otimes1_Q)=\rho_{M\otimes a^*Q}\,t_{c_2;M,Q}.$$
The compact-support comparison lemma fixes $\rho$ as exactly this proper/open refinement arrow. Since $\rho$ is invertible, its inverse also respects these tensor maps, by cancellation. Composing such equations proves the same for comparisons through a common refinement.

proof.text: Now choose the compatible tower supplied in the STATEMENT of the compact-support comparison lemma: compactify $g$ by $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $s:\overline Y\to Z$, and compactify $if$ by $a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$. Put $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, with $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $q:V\to Y$, $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, so $bj=a$. These give the compactifications $(j,q)$ of $f$ and $(a,sp)$ of $gf$. On these choices $\alpha$ is $S_s$ of the CARTESIAN interchange $J_iS_q\to S_pJ_b$, followed by the proper and open compositors. Step 11 has established tensor compatibility of arbitrary refinement comparisons, so passage to this tower, and back from it, now preserves the projection maps as well as $\alpha$.

proof.text:
Expand $t_g$, $S_sJ_i(t_f)$ and $\alpha$ on that tower. Their middle factors are $\gamma_i$, $J_i(\pi_q)$ and $\Gamma$, so step 4 replaces them by $(\Gamma\otimes1)$, $\pi_p$ and $S_p(\gamma_b)$ in the reverse route. Step 3 combines the proper projections for $p,s$; step 2 combines the open tensor maps for $j,b$. Naturality lets these substitutions be whiskered by $S_s$ and $J_j$. Thus both expanded routes are equal, with source $(S_sJ_iS_qJ_jM)\otimes K$ and target $S_{sp}J_a(M\otimes f^*g^*K)$. Returning to tensor factors on the left by the SAME signed symmetry in each occurrence gives
$$\alpha_{g,f,f^*g^*K\otimes M}\,Rg_!(P_{f,g^*K,M})\,P_{g,K,Rf_!M}
=P_{gf,K,M}(1_K\otimes\alpha_{g,f,M}).$$
Step 11 and the refinement compatibility of $\alpha$ in the comparison lemma give this identity on all compactifications, including noncartesian refinements. Each equality was of derived transformations, not merely of their stalk or cohomology maps.
